title: Server-side cursor compaction and tenant-aware response shaping for dashboard query API
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Long-running dashboard queries for multi-tenant analytics (large time ranges + high-cardinality dimensions) are causing high tail latency and expensive read amplification. Existing server cursors keep full per-tenant cursor state in memory and return variable-sized pages which can spike response size and downstream rendering costs. Users see occasional 500ms+ tail spikes on topk/time-series endpoints and the console query cost is increasing with larger cohorts.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and read amplification for dashboard query APIs by implementing (1) server-side cursor compaction to shrink per-cursor memory and GC pressure, and (2) tenant-aware response shaping to bound per-request payload size and apply graceful pagination backpressure. Target: 30-50% reduction in 95th/99th token-read latency and 20% lower read IO for heavy tenants within two weeks of rollout.

Proposed approach: 
- Cursor compaction: Introduce a compacted cursor representation that serializes long-lived cursor state into a compressed, append-only blob stored in a cursor store (redis cluster with blob shards). Keep an in-memory hot-prefix for active requests while evicting cold cursor segments. Implement epoched cursor versions to allow safe compaction during concurrent reads.
- Tenant-aware response shaping: Add a response-shaping layer in the query service that inspects tenant quota and recent request histogram to determine a target payload size (rows or tokens). If query results exceed the target, the service will: (a) return a compact page with a continuation token and metadata about trimmed aggregates, and (b) optionally enqueue a background prefetch for the next page when allowed.
- Read-path optimizations: Use columnar projection for time-series payloads to reduce bytes scanned for trimmed pages, and add a light-weight index hinter that prefers narrow index iterators when tenant shaping is active.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Storing compacted cursor blobs increases storage and introduces a new critical dependency (redis blob store). We mitigate by sharding blobs by tenant and TTLing cursors aggressively.
- Response shaping may change client semantics (smaller pages). We'll expose a clear flag in API metadata ("shaped": true) and provide SDK helpers to transparently page until a stable snapshot is reached.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th latency for dashboard/topk endpoints decreases by >=30% in canary tenants; 99th latency by >=20% in canary tenants.
- Per-request memory for active cursors reduced by >=40% on average on the canary service.
- Error rate not increased; no increase in stale data incidents during canary.
- Client SDK correctly iterates shaped pages in integration tests.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind "cursor_compaction" and "tenant_shaping" flags.
2) Deploy compaction with non-shaping mode first (store blobs but keep full pages). Monitor memory and GC.
3) Enable shaping for 5% of canary tenants with low SLA (nightly jobs, internal teams).
4) Expand to 25% then 100% after meeting metrics threshold.

Metrics to monitor:
- 50/95/99 latency (ms) for dashboard/query endpoints segmented by tenant tier.
- Cursor store ops/sec and average blob size.
- Read IO (GB/day) for canary tenants.
- Rate of client page-retry errors and SDK failures.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for cursor serialization/compaction, epoch concurrency, and version migration.
- Integration test harness that replays production query traces against shaped/unshaped modes and validates consistency and ordering.
- Load test in perf env recreating top-80% tenant workloads.

Dependencies: ENG-27109 (graceful-pagination-fallback-and-lattice-index-coordinator) for fallback semantics; a short-lived infra change to add a redis blob shard (infra ticket created separately).
